why: The model for passing state DOWN a tree: carry the target still to reach (or the sum so far) into each child, and check it only when you arrive at a leaf.
hints: Going from a node to a child, how does the remaining target change?
Pass remaining = targetSum - node.val to both children. At a leaf, the path works exactly when remaining equals the leaf's value.
DFS returning hasPath(left, rem) or hasPath(right, rem), or a stack of (node, sumSoFar). O(n) time, O(h) space.
pitfalls: The path must end at a leaf: a node with one child is not a leaf, so do not stop there.
An empty tree is false even for targetSum = 0.
Values can be negative, so you cannot prune when the running sum passes the target.
